title_en: Real Estate Credit Over Yield at Invesco – Charlie Rose (EP.519)
title_zh: Invesco 房地产信用：信用优先于收益率 — Charlie Rose (EP.519)
subtitle_zh: Invesco 房地产信用全球主管 Charlie Rose 谈“先信用后收益”的放贷之道、回避数据中心与 AI 敞口，以及 2022-23 调整的教训。
summary_zh: 本期 Capital Allocators 是一集赞助特别节目（sponsored insight），Ted Seides 对话 Invesco 房地产信用全球主管 Charlie Rose——他管理着一个规模约 850 亿美元的全球平台，此前在 UC Berkeley Fisher 房地产中心做过研究、在 Canyon Partners 做了八年贯穿资本结构的投资。核心命题是信用优先于收益率（credit over yield）与以不动产为先（property first）的承保哲学：Invesco 约四分之三的借款人是回头客，投委会上发起人、信用承保、收购与股权资产管理团队协作发言。节目最具争议性的一点，是 Rose 明确表态不做数据中心贷款——超大规模（hyperscale）项目往往只有单一租户，五到二十年后空间可复用性存疑、存在功能性贬值（functional obsolescence）且缺乏替代用途，剔除这类 AI 敞口有助于维持资产的低相关性。他还复盘写字楼在加息周期中前所未有的价值毁灭、工业与多户住宅的 sheds 与 beds 主题，以及 2022-23 房地产调整与问题贷款管理的教训（一笔 2020 年的酒店贷款最终被全额偿还）。他坦言 2022 年 12 月的首次已实现亏损是一种解放，让他以更谦卑的眼光审视成败中的运气成分。

turns.en: I'll share with you a controversial position that we've taken. We are not lending on data centers. It is a tempting sector to lend to in this environment. The supply of opportunity is immense. The yields are interesting on the face of it. We're seeing valuations of these tech firms explode in this environment. However, we believe that there's fundamental binary risk in data center investments. In the hyperscaled situations, you oftentimes have a single tenant.
turns.zh: 我来分享一个我们所持的有争议的立场：我们不做数据中心的贷款。在当前环境下，这是一个很诱人的放贷领域。机会的供给是巨大的，表面上的收益率也很有吸引力，我们看到这些科技公司的估值在这个环境下暴涨。然而，我们相信数据中心投资存在根本性的二元风险（binary risk）。在超大规模（hyperscale）的情形下，你往往只有一个租户。

turns.en: They may be investment grade today. It's unclear to us how reusable that space may be or what the functional obsolescence considerations may be five, 10, 20 years from now for that real estate. And there's no alternative use. A lot of different segments of the investable universe have some meaningful exposure to AI. If we can remove that exposure from our portfolio, that will help maintain that low correlation profile of our asset class.
turns.zh: 它们今天可能是投资级的。对我们来说不清楚的是，五年、十年、二十年后，那类地产的空间可复用性如何，功能性贬值（functional obsolescence）有哪些考量。而且它没有替代用途。历史上，可投资范围的许多板块都对 AI 有一定的实质性敞口。如果我们能把那个敞口从组合中剔除，将有助于维持我们这类资产的低相关性特征。

turns.en: I'm Ted Sides and this is Capital Allocators. My guest on today's show is Charlie Rose, the global head of real estate credit at Invesco, where he oversees an $85 billion global platform.
turns.zh: 我是 Ted Seides，这里是 Capital Allocators。今天节目的嘉宾是 Charlie Rose，Invesco 房地产信用全球主管，他管理着一个 850 亿美元的全球平台。

turns.en: Before joining Invesco, Charlie worked in real estate as an academic researcher, Jack of all trades through the financial crisis, and investor up and down the capital stack for eight years at Canyon Partners. Our conversation covers Invesco's credit over yield approach, property first underwriting, collaborative work inside the firm, and relationship based focus.
turns.zh: 在加入 Invesco 之前，Charlie 在房地产领域做过学术研究，金融危机期间做过样样都干的万金油，并在 Canyon Partners 做了八年贯穿资本结构上下游的投资。我们的对话涵盖 Invesco 信用优先于收益率（credit over yield）的方法、以不动产为先（property first）的承保、公司内部的协作，以及关系为重的定位。

turns.en: We discuss sourcing through repeat borrowers, risk management, portfolio construction, contrarian calls, including avoiding data centers and AI exposure, and sheds and beds theme of industrial and multifamily loans. We close with lessons from the 2022-23 real estate correction, managing troubled loans, and how Invesco is using AI to improve investment decisions.
turns.zh: 我们讨论了通过回头客借款人获取资产、风险管理、组合构建、逆向判断——包括回避数据中心和 AI 敞口——以及工业与多户住宅（multifamily）贷款的 sheds 与 beds（仓库与床位）主题。最后谈到了 2022-23 年房地产调整的教训、问题贷款管理，以及 Invesco 如何用 AI 改善投资决策。

turns.en: I'd love you to take me back to where your initial interest in real estate started. I grew up in a small town about 45 minutes east of Seattle, Falls City, Washington, where it rains 30% more than in the city of Seattle.
turns.zh: 我想请你回到你最初对房地产产生兴趣的起点。——我在一个小镇长大，西雅图东边大约 45 分钟车程，华盛顿州 Falls City，那里的雨比西雅图市区还多 30%。

turns.en: Simple life, great hard-working community. I saw a few examples of people in our community who made it out, had done well for themselves. The pivotal moment for me was when my family had an opportunity to live in Switzerland in sixth grade. It completely opened my eyes to the world and the built environment, set me on a different trajectory. I was an English major in undergrad. I had no internships in commercial real estate in college. I had this vague idea that
turns.zh: 简单的生活，勤劳肯干的社区。我见过社区里几个走出去、做得很成功的例子。对我而言的转折点是六年级时我们家有机会去瑞士居住。那完全打开了我的眼界，让我看到世界与建成环境，把我引向了一条不同的人生轨迹。我本科读的是英语专业，大学期间没有任何商业地产的实习。我只有一个模糊的想法，觉得……

turns.en: real estate would be an interesting career path. I had no idea what that meant. I applied to pretty much anything that I could see that had the words real estate in it. Eventually, I landed a job working for Ken Rosen, the chair of the Fisher Center of Real Estate at UC Berkeley as a research analyst. He needed someone who was a good writer. I spent three years working for Ken, learning about what fundamentally drives demand and supply in the real estate markets
turns.zh: ……房地产会是一条有趣的职业路径，但我完全不知道那意味着什么。我几乎申请了所有我看到带“房地产”字样的工作。最后我在 Ken Rosen 手下找到了一份工作，他是 UC Berkeley Fisher 房地产中心的主任，我在那里担任研究分析师。他需要一个文笔好的人。我为 Ken 工作了三年，学习从根本上驱动房地产市场需求和供给的力量

turns.en: that has been the basis for my career. During that time, our clients were investment banks, commercial banks, private equity funds, home builders. I saw what our clients were experiencing, the decisions that they were making. I went back to business school and then got on the buy side.
turns.zh: ……这成为我整个职业生涯的基础。那期间，我们的客户是投资银行、商业银行、私募股权基金、住宅建筑商。我看到了客户在经历什么、他们在做什么决策。后来我回去读了商学院，然后进入了买方。

turns.en: What was your trajectory from the interest in real estate to landing where you have on the credit side? One of the things that gives me a lot of pleasure in my role is having the opportunity to speak with young people who are just exploring careers in real estate or are early in their careers.
turns.zh: 你从对房地产的兴趣，到落脚在信用这一侧，轨迹是怎样的？——在我的角色里，让我很享受的一件事，是能跟刚开始探索房地产职业、或者职业早期的年轻人交流。

turns.en: I always share the same advice. One, of course, work hard. Find that opportunity where you can put in long hours, get maximal exposure early in your career. The other piece of advice is be open-minded. Be ready to leap at opportunity when it presents itself, even if it's not exactly what you expected that opportunity to be. When I graduated from business school, I thought that I was going to be a real estate developer. Many people who enter the commercial
turns.zh: 我分享的都是同样的建议。第一，当然要努力工作。找到那些能让你投入长时间、在职业早期获得最大化曝光的机会。另一条建议是保持开放心态。当机会出现时，要准备好扑上去，即使它并不是你原本期待的那种机会。商学院毕业时，我以为自己会去做房地产开发商。很多进入商业……

turns.en: real estate business come with that expectation early on. Who doesn't want to drive down the street and point out the window of the car and tell your kids, I built that tower. That was an alluring idea. The opportunities that were presented to me were different. I graduated business school in 2008, not a dissimilar environment from when I graduated undergrad in 03. I was undergrad in the Bay Area during the tech rec. Oh wait, we were glad to have any job in real estate
turns.zh: ……地产行业的人最初都抱着这样的期待。谁不想开车走在街上，指着窗外告诉孩子：那栋楼是我建的？那是一个很诱人的想法。但摆在我面前的机会不一样。我 2008 年商学院毕业，那环境跟我 03 年本科毕业时相差无几。我在湾区读本科时正赶上科技衰退。哦对了，当时在房地产领域能找到任何工作我们都很知足……

turns.en: at the time. I worked for a real estate holding company. I was working on workouts, negotiating with lenders. I thought I was going to be doing acquisitions when I took the job. There were no acquisitions around. At one point, my boss said, we're shutting down one of our regional offices.
turns.zh: ……我那时在一家房地产控股公司工作，做的其实是贷款处置（workout），跟贷款方谈判。我入职时以为自己做的是收购，但当时根本没有收购可做。有一次我老板说，我们要关掉一个区域办公室了。

turns.en: Could you sell the office furniture? I would do whatever was necessary to keep that job. From there, I took a job at Canyon Partners. Canyon had raised the $1.1 billion fund and was staffing up to take advantage of distress. We were investing up and down the capital stack.
turns.zh: 你能把办公家具卖掉吗？为了保住那份工作，我什么都愿意做。从那以后，我加入了 Canyon Partners。Canyon 刚募了一只 11 亿美元的基金，正在招兵买马以抓住困境资产的机会。我们在资本结构的上下游都做投资。

turns.en: We were buying debt, recapping deals, senior loans, pref equity, eventually moving back into common equity. That was a great experience because it created optionality in my career later on. I had equity experience, debt experience, distressed experience. I didn't expect that I would end up being a lender at that time. I thought eventually I would be a developer. Fast forward eight years, I got a call from some of my now colleagues at Invesco Real Estate. We had clubbed on the
turns.zh: 我们买债务、重组交易、做高级贷款、优先股权（pref equity），后来又做回普通股股权。那是一段很棒的经历，因为它为我后来的职业创造了选择性。我有股权经验、债务经验、困境资产经验。我那时并没有想到自己最终会做一个贷款人，我以为自己迟早会去做开发。八年后，我接到 Invesco 房地产几位如今同事的电话。我们曾经联合参与过……

turns.en: acquisition of the largest subperforming loan sale that Bank of America made coming out of the global financial crisis. They wanted to scale a credit business. They were looking for the right person to do that. I seized on the opportunity because the Invesco platform is characterized by information sharing, collaboration, and great client relationships. I believe that we could build something special here at Invesco. As you made that decision to go over to Invesco from Canyon,
turns.zh: ……一笔收购，那是 Bank of America 在全球金融危机后出售的最大一笔弱级贷款（sub-performing loan）资产包。他们想把信用业务规模化，正在找合适的人来做。我抓住了这个机会，因为 Invesco 平台的特点是信息共享、协作和出色的客户关系。我相信我们能在 Invesco 打造一些特别的东西。——在你做出去 Invesco 而不是留在 Canyon 的决定时……

turns.en: other than the high-level feel-good nature of the buzzwords you might use to describe the platform, how did the platform impact how you thought about building this business?
turns.zh: ……除了那些描述平台的高大上流行语带来的良好感觉之外，这个平台是如何影响你思考搭建这个业务的？

turns.en: Invesco has a distinct culture. It's hard to describe culture in a conversation like this. You need to be in the trenches with people to experience that culture. In our business, we can all think about organizations where there's a lot of competition between investment professionals, a lot of pressure that comes out of that. Invesco has, at the core of the culture, a collaboration approach. Our CEO of private markets calls that IQ compounding. He has been a
turns.zh: Invesco 有一种独特的文化。在这样的对话里很难描述文化，你得和人们一起在前线并肩作战，才能体验那种文化。在我们这个行业，大家都能想到一些组织，投资专业人士之间竞争激烈，由此带来很大压力。Invesco 文化的内核是一种协作方式。我们私募市场业务的 CEO 把这叫做 IQ 复利（IQ compounding）。他一直是一位……

turns.en: tremendous leader in evidencing to our people that we do better when we work together. That was what I bought into as we started this credit business, that I would be surrounded by an amazing team of people that had my back and were supporting me in everything that I was doing.
turns.zh: ……非常出色的领导者，用事实证明给我们的员工：一起协作时我们做得更好。当我开始做这个信用业务时，我看重的正是这一点——我会被一群了不起的人围绕，他们会为我兜底，支持我做的每一件事。

turns.en: That's fundamental to what we've built here. When we talk about our Invesco edge as lenders in the market, we talk about how we're a relationship-based lender. Our credit approach, which we call credit-over-yield investing, the third key aspect to our Invesco edge is our property-first approach to lending. We only lend on the type of real estate that we own on the equity side of the business.
turns.zh: 这是我们在 Invesco 建立的一切的根本。当我们谈到作为贷款人在市场上的 Invesco 优势（Invesco edge）时，我们会说自己是一个关系型贷款人。我们的信用方法称为信用优先于收益率（credit-over-yield）投资。Invesco 优势的第三个关键要素是以不动产为先（property-first）的放贷方式。我们只在我们自己股权端持有的那类房地产上做贷款。

turns.en: We ensure that we do that by having a process whereby our loan originators are out in the market talking to our repeat borrowers. About three-quarters of our borrowers are repeat borrowers.
turns.zh: 我们怎么做到这一点？靠这样一个流程：我们的贷款发起人到市场上与我们的回头客借款人交流。大约四分之三的借款人是回头客。

turns.en: They're identifying opportunities that fit the box on paper. They're immediately bringing in their colleagues whose job is to buy real estate in the given market and property-type combination. By the time we get to investment committee, we've had a true collaborative approach between our originator, our credit underwriters, our acquisitions team, and our equity asset management team who's providing a lot of insight from what they're seeing in our existing
turns.zh: 他们在纸面上筛选符合标准的投资机会，然后马上把负责在特定市场与特定物业类型组合里做收购的同事拉进来。等我们走到投资委员会时，我们的发起人、信用承保团队、收购团队，以及股权资产管理部门之间已经真正协作过了，后者从我们现有……

turns.en: owned portfolio. That investment committee, all of those people speak up and are expected to evidence that they've been engaged in the process and they're supportive of the transaction.
turns.zh: ……持有的组合中贡献了大量洞察。在投委会上，所有人都会发言，并且需要证明他们参与了流程、支持这笔交易。

turns.en: Today, we're one of the foremost active debt fund lenders in the US. If the equity side of the house is pursuing an acquisition of a property, they're the runner-up on that transaction. One of our competitors is awarded the transaction. Then we on the credit side jump right in behind them.
turns.zh: 如今，我们是全美最领先的主动债务基金贷款人之一。如果自家股权端在追逐一笔物业收购，他们往往是那笔交易的落选方。我们的某个竞争对手赢得了交易，然后我们信用端就紧跟其后。

turns.en: We'll quote the debt typically have a head start on our competition. In other instances, where we're working with our relationship borrowers and our relationship borrowers are generally our peers, 90-plus percent of our borrowers are institutional groups. If you think of a big private equity manager with a real estate business, they're most likely one of our borrowers. When they bring us a de novo transaction, we're working side by side with the equity colleagues to get
turns.zh: 我们会报债务的价，通常比竞争对手快人一步。在其他情形下，我们和关系型借款人合作，而我们的关系型借款人通常就是我们的同业——90% 以上的借款人是机构型客户。你想想那些大型私募股权管理人旗下做房地产的，他们很可能就是我们的借款人。当他们带着全新交易（de novo）找我们时，我们与股权端的同事并肩工作，以获取……

turns.zh: ……他们的洞察，因为他们每天都在这些市场的第一线，能帮助我们更好地为我们看到的机会承保风险。

turns.en: If you work backwards at second point, credit over yield, what do you mean by that? When we are investing, we identify outperformance as hitting the target returns that we have established, then outperforming on credit quality. We define outperformance as having better quality sponsors, higher quality real estate, lower advance rates or loan to value ratios, higher cash coverage, and better covenant packages. When we are sitting in our Monday morning
turns.zh: 我们倒回到第二点，信用优先于收益率，你说的是什么意思？——当我们投资时，我们把跑赢定义为达到我们设定的目标回报，然后在信用质量上超越。我们定义的超额表现是：更好的发起人质量、更高质量的房地产、更低的抵押率或贷款价值比（loan-to-value）、更高的现金覆盖率、更好的条款包（covenant package）。当我们在周一早上……

turns.en: pipeline call talking about the opportunities in front of us and the competitive dynamic, our default is always to say, we're going to lean in on pricing rather than leaning in on leverage or structure. If I have my choice, I'm going to try to win business by being more efficiently priced than my peer, rather than winning business by offering a couple million dollars extra proceeds. As you look at that set of criteria,
turns.zh: ……的管线（pipeline）电话会上讨论眼前的机会和竞争态势时，我们的默认立场永远是在定价上让步，而不在杠杆或结构上让步。如果由我选择，我会试图通过比同行定价更高效来赢得业务，而不是通过多给几百万美元的贷款金额来赢得业务。当你看看这一套标准……

turns.en: it lends itself to higher quality assets. You would also think by nature of that underwriting, lower yields, maybe lower returns than peers. How do you think of positioning yourself as a strategy if most of what you're trying to underwrite is safer than what other people are?
turns.zh: ……这套标准天然指向更高质量的资产。你也会觉得，按那种承保方式的性质，收益率更低，回报也许也低于同行。如果你要承保的大多数东西都比别人更安全，你怎么看待自己作为一个策略的定位？

turns.en: As a credit investor, the number one most important part of my job is preserving principle or protecting invested capital. Downside protection is more important than optimizing yield. They're both important. If we can't get that downside protection piece, then the yield piece becomes irrelevant. That's our starting point. We have a risk-based approach to underwriting opportunity. We're looking at a whole swath of potential risks, whether that's
turns.zh: 作为一名信用投资人，我工作中最重要的头等大事是保全本金、保护投入的资本。下行保护比优化收益率更重要。两者都重要，但如果我们做不到下行保护，收益率就无关紧要了。那是我们的起点。我们用基于风险的方法来承保机会，审视一整套潜在的风险，无论是……

turns.en: physical property risk, climate risk, insurance risk, market risk, counterparty risk. We then believe if we can assemble a portfolio of high-quality credits, we will minimize default risk, minimize risk of loss. We can prudently use our broad balance sheet relationships from our 2.4 trillion AUM overall platform to optimize the type of leverage that we get against our loans and deliver the types of returns that our investors expect.
turns.zh: ……物业实体风险、气候风险、保险风险、市场风险、交易对手风险。我们相信，如果能组装一个高质量信用的组合，就会把违约风险、损失风险降到最低。我们可以审慎地利用整体 2.4 万亿美元 AUM 平台带来的广泛资产负债表关系，来优化我们贷款所获得的杠杆类型，交付投资人所期待的回报。

turns.en: What are the levers that you use to drive returns knowing you're trying to avoid the left tail? One of the most important things that we can do to ensure that we are, A, maintaining our credit over yield posture, and B, not getting ground to the very last basis point from a pricing perspective, is focus on those relationships. Our relationships today are roughly 100 borrowers in good standing. Over 70% of the loans that we will originate this year
turns.zh: 你明知自己在规避左尾，那么用来驱动回报的杠杆是什么？——要确保我们一是维持信用优先于收益率的姿态，二是在定价上不被挤压到最后一个基点，最重要的事情之一就是专注于那些关系。我们现在的关系大约是 100 家处于良好状态的借款人。今年我们即将发起的贷款里，70% 以上……

turns.en: will be loans that we characterize as off-market or preferentially sourced loans with those borrowers. If we can find opportunities where we've developed these constructive relationships, we can avoid the heavily bid auction processes. We believe that we can set up true win-win transactions with our borrowers where we're achieving a fair yield for our investors.
turns.zh: ……将是我们与这些借款人做的、我们称为场外（off-market）或优先来源的贷款。如果我们能在这种富有建设性的关系中找到机会，就能避开竞标激烈的拍卖流程。我们相信能与借款人建立真正的双赢交易：我们为投资人取得公平的收益率，

turns.en: They're getting certainty of execution, flexibility, fair pricing, and a relationship which is going to give them positive leverage in multiple ways over many years.
turns.zh: 他们获得的则是执行的确定性、灵活性、公平的定价，以及一段会在很多年里从多方面给他们带来正向杠杆的关系。

turns.en: When one of those hundred investors brings you a new opportunity, what are the things you're looking at to avoid that you see that could be a risk or could cause a loss relative to another property? There are a lot we've spent a lot of time thinking about. Is there any potential binary risk in this credit? We're generally looking to lend on properties that have an attractive cash flow profile, a diversified tenant base or diversified demand for that property. We're looking to lend
turns.zh: 当这 100 家借款人中的一家给你带来一个新机会时，你会看什么东西，以识别出相对于另一处物业，这可能构成风险或导致亏损的地方？——有很多，我们花了很多时间思考。这笔信用里是否存在任何潜在的二元风险？我们通常寻找的放贷对象，是具有吸引力的现金流特征、租户基础或需求多元化的物业。我们希望放贷于……

turns.en: in markets that have evidenced healthy liquidity throughout market cycles historically and where we think that fundamental liquidity profile will hold up going forward. I'll share with you a controversial position that we've taken. We are not lending on data centers. It is a tempting sector to lend to in this environment. The supply of opportunity is immense. The yields are interesting on the face of it. We're seeing valuations of these tech firms explode in this
turns.zh: ……在历史市场周期中证明了流动性健康、并且我们认为其基础流动性特征在未来也能维持的市场。我来分享一个我们所持的有争议的立场：我们不做数据中心的贷款。在当前环境下，这是一个很诱人的放贷领域。机会的供给是巨大的，表面上的收益率很有吸引力，我们看到这些科技公司的估值在这个环境下暴涨。

turns.en: environment. However, we believe that there's fundamental binary risk in data center investments in the hyperscaled situations you oftentimes have a single tenant. They may be investment grade today. It's unclear to us how reusable that space may be or what the functional obsolescence considerations may be five, 10, 20 years from now for that real estate. There's no alternative use. That goes completely in the face of our approach consistent with the credit over yield
turns.zh: 然而，我们相信数据中心投资存在根本性的二元风险。在超大规模的情形下，你往往只有一个租户。他们今天可能是投资级的。我们不清楚的是，五年、十年、二十年后，那类地产的空间可复用性如何，功能性贬值有哪些考量，而且没有替代用途。这与我们的方法完全背道而驰——信用优先于收益率的授权就是要规避二元风险。另一层原因是，我们认为很多投资人并不希望我们投数据中心。房地产信用的特征是对大多数其他资产类别的低相关性，

turns.en: mandate of avoiding binary risk. The other piece of it is we don't think many of our investors want us to be investing in data centers. Real estate credit is characterized by a low correlation to most other asset classes, low correlation to any public market, fixed income or equity asset classes. Interestingly, a sub point to correlation to private equity, private credit, real estate equity, real estate credit has been a good diversifier in both a broad portfolio, also in an
turns.zh: 对任何公开市场的固定收益或股票资产类别的低相关性。有趣的是，把私募股权、私募信用、房地产股权的相关性作为次要点来看，房地产信用一直是一个很好的分散化来源，既在大的组合里，也在一个……

turns.en: Alts portfolio. Historically, a lot of different segments of the investable universe have some meaningful exposure to AI. If we can remove that exposure from our portfolio, that will help maintain that low correlation profile of our asset class. What are some of the opportunities where you are leaning in? We will have our most productive year from a deployment perspective this year.
turns.zh: ……另类资产（Alts）组合里。历史上，可投资范围的许多板块都对 AI 有一定的实质性敞口。如果我们能把那个敞口从组合中剔除，将有助于维持我们这类资产的低相关性特征。——你们在往哪些机会上发力？今年我们的投放将会是有史以来产量最大的一年。

turns.en: Year to date, we have either closed or committed to well over $5 billion of loans which will exceed our prior record for deployment. That is coming predominantly from two underlying themes. One is a theme that has been present in the market for a number of years. Banks are less active as a percentage of the overall real estate debt market than they have been historically. Real estate credit is the fourth largest fixed income asset class in the US. It's a $6 trillion asset class.
turns.zh: 年初至今，我们已关闭或承诺了远超 50 亿美元的贷款，这将超过我们此前的投放纪录。这主要来自两个底层主题。一个是市场上已经存在多年的主题：银行在整个房地产债务市场中的活跃度占比低于历史水平。房地产信用是美国第四大固定收益资产类别，是一个 6 万亿美元的资产类别。

turns.en: That's not to say that the banks are not active in real estate credit, they are. Historically, the banks were 51% of the market prior to COVID. Today, they're roughly a third of the market.
turns.zh: 这并非说银行在房地产信用上不活跃——他们仍然活跃。历史上，在 COVID 之前银行占市场的 51%，如今他们大概只占三分之一。

turns.en: That's left this gap that debt funds and alternative lenders such as ourselves have been filling. The second underlying theme which is coming into play this year and we expect to be sustained over the next couple of years is an elevated maturity environment. I don't necessarily talk about a wall of maturities. We are expecting $3 trillion of real estate debt maturities over the next five years. This year is five years after the prior peak of loan originations in
turns.zh: 这就留下了一个缺口，债务基金和像我们这样的另类贷款人一直在填补。第二个底层主题从今年开始显现，我们预计会在未来几年持续：一个高到期量环境。我不一定说“到期墙”。我们预计未来五年将有 3 万亿美元的房地产债务到期。今年是上一个贷款发放峰值年份

turns.en: 2021. You're seeing a lot of loans come due. That is driving a material increase in refinance activity. More of the loans that we are originating today are refinance loans than we've seen historically. We're active along the coast. We're active in the sunbelt. We're active in Europe.
turns.zh: 2021 年之后的第五年，你会看到大量贷款到期。这正在驱动再融资活动的显著增加。今天我们发起的贷款里，再融资贷款的占比比历史上任何时候都高。我们在沿海活跃，在阳光带（Sunbelt）活跃，在欧洲也活跃。

turns.en: The vast majority of our volume is industrial, multifamily, and variations on those two themes, beds and sheds. What is it about those two that attract your attention?
turns.zh: 我们绝大部分业务量是工业和多户住宅，以及这两个主题的变体——beds and sheds（床位与仓库）。这两者有什么吸引你们的地方？

turns.en: Industrial and multifamily are the most liquid property types in the US. In Europe, logistics is one of the most liquid property types. The multifamily market is less mature in Europe. We like the liquidity profile that is helpful for us in underwriting multiple sources of repayment. It also means that our relationship borrowers are pretty active in those two spaces specifically. When we talk about logistics, we're generally talking about multi-tenant
turns.zh: 工业和多户住宅是美国流动性最好的物业类型。在欧洲，物流仓储是流动性最好的物业类型之一，多户住宅市场在欧洲还不够成熟。我们喜欢这种流动性特征，它有助于我们为多重还款来源做承保。这也意味着我们的关系型借款人恰恰在这两个领域非常活跃。当我们说到物流时，我们通常说的是多租户……

turns.en: logistics. Oftentimes, we're financing portfolios that are geographically diversified. You end up getting similar characteristics between logistics and multifamily in as much as you have a granular underlying set of tenants, which provides some diversification if a certain industry is experiencing headwinds that won't mean that we'll see wholesale weakness in our underlying tenant profile.
turns.zh: ……物流仓储。很多时候，我们在为地理上分散的资产组合做融资。物流和多户住宅呈现出相似的特征：底层租户足够细碎，带来一定的分散化——即使某个行业遇到逆风，也不意味着我们的底层租户盘会出现全面走弱。

turns.en: Curious to ask you about office. Post-COVID, there was this question of where do office occupancies settle in in major cities? What have you seen in the office market over the last bunch of years? We spent so much time talking about office, and it's a relatively small part of the institutional universe today. It was a larger part historically. Office looms large in our conscience. These are the tall buildings, the shiny towers in our CBDs. A lot of us have spent a
turns.zh: 我想问问写字楼。疫情之后有一个问题：大城市的写字楼入驻率最终会稳定在哪里？过去几年你在写字楼市场上看到了什么？——我们花了太多时间谈论写字楼，而它在今天的机构可投资范围里只占相对小的部分，历史上占比更大。写字楼在我们心目中分量很重，那些是我们 CBD 里的高楼、闪亮的塔楼。我们很多人把职业生涯的大量时间都……

turns.en: lot of our careers working in these buildings. What we saw coming out of COVID, the straw that broke the camel's back was the rate-hiking cycle, was an unprecedented amount of value destruction in an unprecedentedly short period of time for any single property type.
turns.zh: ……花在了这些楼里。疫情之后我们看到的是，压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草是加息周期——对单一物业类型而言，在前所未有的短时间内发生了前所未有的价值毁灭。

turns.en: What we saw in office was far faster and more acute than what we saw in the regional mall sector earlier in our careers. It has been painful for many in the industry. Today, there's more clarity around what office is in demand, what office is not in demand, more clarity around values.
turns.zh: 我们在写字楼上看到的，比我们职业生涯早期在区域购物中心行业看到的要快得多、猛烈得多。这对行业里很多人来说是痛苦的。如今，关于什么样的写字楼有需求、什么样的没有，以及关于估值，都有了更清晰的认知。

turns.en: Office buildings are selling in this environment. We can peg values with better certainty. For much of the last five years, we wouldn't touch office. The first reason for that was if there's one thing I hate as a lender more than anything else, it's uncertainty.
turns.zh: 写字楼在这个环境下是有人买的，我们可以更有把握地锚定价值。过去五年的大部分时间里，我们不碰写字楼。第一个原因是：如果说作为贷款人有什么比不确定性更让我深恶痛绝，那没有了。

turns.en: It was difficult to underwrite demand, rents, and ultimately values in an environment where most players were on the sidelines. Today, office is more underwriteable, at least for the good stuff.
turns.zh: 在大多数玩家都作壁上观的环境里，你很难为需求、租金、最终是估值做承保。如今，写字楼更可承保了，至少好的那部分是。

turns.en: There are some unique challenges to office that make it a tougher asset class for us to underwrite. One is it is a very capital-intensive asset class. You think about how much it costs to build out a new office suite, then the fact that you have to continually do so as Lisa's role introduces a high capex burden, which is challenging and optimizing returns.
turns.zh: 写字楼有一些独特的挑战，使它成为对我们来说更难承保的资产类别。一是它是非常资本密集的资产类别。你想想新建一套办公室的装修成本有多高，然后你还得不断重复投入——租约到期续租会带来很高的资本开支负担，这让优化回报变得困难。

turns.en: Secondly, you tend to have more GDP correlation. In many instances, some binary exposure to tenancy. We have made one office loan this year. Granted, we're going to make well more than 50 loans this year. That is the first step for us post-recovery. The office loan that we made was in the San Francisco CBD.
turns.zh: 第二，你往往有更高的 GDP 相关性，很多情况下对租户还存在某种二元敞口。我们今年只做了一笔写字楼贷款——当然，我们今年会做远超 50 笔贷款。那是我们在复苏之后的第一步。我们做的那笔写字楼贷款在旧金山的 CBD。

turns.en: Would love to hear more about your underwriting process with your team when a potential loan crosses your desk. What do you guys do? The first step is an email followed by a phone call from someone with whom we have an existing relationship. They're going to send us some basic information, loan amount, property type, location, key credit metrics, the leverage ratio that they're seeking, and the cash flow profile
turns.zh: 我很想多听听，当一笔潜在贷款来到你面前时，你和团队的承保流程是怎样的，你们都做什么？——第一步是一封邮件加一个电话，来自一个与我们已有关系的人。他们会给我们一些基本信息：贷款金额、物业类型、位置、关键信用指标、他们寻求的杠杆率、以及

turns.en: of the asset. With that basic information, we can weed out the vast majority of loans and say, hey, this is not a fit for us for one reason or another. It's too big. It's too small. Maybe it's going to go fixed rate. Most of our loans are floating rate. For those loans that do fit our box, we have a team that is responsible for underwriting the investment. The team is led by a senior originator. Our originators have had prior careers either at banks, insurance companies,
turns.zh: ……该资产的现金流特征。靠这些基本信息，我们就能筛掉绝大多数贷款，说：嘿，因为这样或那样的原因，这不合适我们。规模太大，太小，也许它要转固定利率——我们的大部分贷款是浮动的。对那些符合我们标准的贷款，有一个团队负责承保这笔投资，由一位资深发起人牵头。我们的发起人在加入 Invesco 之前，要么在银行、保险公司……

turns.en: or other debt funds before joining Invesco. They're supported by associates and analysts who are responsible for running all of the numbers. They're actively bringing in experts from other parts of our business to opine on the underwriting. We underwrite the underlying collateral as if we were buying the real estate. Our associates and analysts use the exact same cash flow model that their peers on the equity side of our business do.
turns.zh: ……或者其他债务基金有过往职业经历。他们由经理（associate）和分析师支持，后者负责跑所有数字。他们会积极地从公司其他业务部门请来专家对承保发表意见。我们对底层抵押物的承保，就好像我们自己要买这处房地产一样。我们的经理和分析师用的现金流模型，与我们业务股权端同行的完全一样。

turns.en: We then determine what we think the loan-to-value ratio is. That may not be the same as what the appraiser says it is. We like to have our own view formed. We'll spend a lot of time in the market.
turns.zh: 然后我们形成自己对贷款价值比的判断，那可能和评估师给出的不一样。我们喜欢先形成自己的观点，会花大量时间泡在市场里。

turns.en: We walk both the assets we're lending on as well as the market. Typically, we have boots on the ground across our organization in most of these markets. We have a two-step investment committee process. Our first investment committee is before we issue a term sheet to our borrower.
turns.zh: 我们会实地走访我们放贷的资产，也会走访整个市场。通常我们在这些市场上的大多数都有组织的现场团队。我们有两步投资委员会流程。第一次投委会是在我们向借款人发出条款书（term sheet）之前。

turns.en: We believe that it's critically important that once we issue a term sheet, we can offer a very high certainty of execution for our borrowers. It would be an extremely unusual situation where if we issue a term sheet, we're unable to close on the transaction. If we sign the term sheet, then we go back to investment committee after we have received a whole series of third-party reports. We send out specialists who are MAI appraisers to do a formal appraisal. We have
turns.zh: 我们认为这一点至关重要：一旦我们发出条款书，就必须为借款人提供极高的执行确定性。如果我们发了条款书却没能成交，那会是极其反常的情况。签署条款书后，在我们收到一整套第三方报告之后，我们会再回到投委会。我们派出持有 MAI 资格的评估师去做正式评估，还会做……

turns.en: physical property inspections. Organizations that have construction specialists on their team, they're going out making sure that the roof plumbing and the electrical is all in good shape.
turns.zh: ……物业的物理检查。那些团队里有建筑专家的机构，他们会出去检查屋顶、管道和电路是否都状况良好。

turns.en: If it's a seismically active zone, we'll have a seismic expert come in and identify how much risk there is of physical damage in a seismic event. Similarly, in a wind zone, a hurricane-prone environment, we do flood studies. We do environmental studies. Once all that's done, all of those reports are reported back to investment committee. In most instances, there aren't any major surprises. If there is a major surprise from a third party, we're addressing
turns.zh: 如果处于地震活跃带，我们会请地震专家来识别地震事件中发生物理损毁的风险有多大。类似地，在风区、飓风易发环境，我们会做洪水研究，也会做环境研究。所有这些完成后，所有报告都会回报投委会。大多数情况下不会有大的意外。如果第三方发现了重大意外，我们会……

turns.en: that with our borrower. Maybe we're adjusting our proceeds. Maybe we're adding some structure. Or there have been a few instances where we've found something with the underlying real estate where we've gone back to our borrower. They've changed their decision on the investment. They've sought to have a price reduction or even dropped the acquisition opportunity.
turns.zh: ……与借款人一起处理。可能是调整我们的贷款金额，可能是增加一些结构。也有过几次，我们在底层房地产发现了问题，回到借款人那里后，他们改变了对这笔投资的决定，寻求降价，甚至干脆放弃了这个收购机会。

turns.en: I'm curious about the pattern recognition of the financial work compared to the on-the-ground work. Whether it's your team kicking the tires or experts you're sending out, the signals that you get on the ground and how you integrate that into a financial modeling and supply and demand framework.
turns.zh: 我很好奇，财务工作和实地工作之间，模式识别是怎么结合的。不管是你的团队亲自去看资产，还是你派出去的专家，你在实地得到的信号，以及你们如何把它整合进财务建模和供需框架。

turns.en: We are looking for information that is unique and not publicly available. There are a lot of information asymmetries in the private markets, generally speaking and in private real estate.
turns.zh: 我们寻找的是独特的、公开渠道拿不到的信息。总体来说，在私募市场、在私人房地产里，存在着大量的信息不对称。

turns.en: There are instances where we're leveraging that boots-on-the-ground expertise to give us helpful forward indicators. Let me give you an example. A couple of years ago, we were underwriting an office building in the Bay Area. Initially, our originator said, this is a slam dunk. We own an office building in the same office park. The office building that we own has good occupancy. It looks like these guys are buying it at a basis, not dissimilar to our
turns.zh: 有些时候，我们会利用这种一线实地专长来获得有用的前瞻指标。让我举个例子。几年前，我们在承保湾区的一栋写字楼。最初我们的发起人说，这是一笔稳赢的交易：我们自己在同一个办公园区持有一栋写字楼，那栋楼出租率很好，看起来他们买入的成本基础跟我们的……

turns.en: basis, full steam ahead. When our asset manager got involved in the underwriting, they said, you guys might want to slow down a little bit here because we have not had a single tenant tour, our building, that we own in this office park for the last 12 months. What we're observing is that all of the tenants in the market are wanting to be on the other side of the sub-market, close to the Caltrain Station. There's little demand in this particular pocket that led us
turns.zh: ……差不多，全速推进。但当我们的资产管理者加入承保时，他们说：你们可能得慢一点，因为在过去 12 个月里，我们在这个办公园区自己持有的那栋楼，一个来看房的租户都没有。我们观察到的是，市场上所有租户都想去这个子市场的另一头，靠近 Caltrain 火车站的那一侧。这个特定片区没什么需求，这让我们……

turns.en: to take a much more conservative approach on rent, absorption, and occupancy for this building, which ultimately made us not competitive, despite the fact that all of the publicly available market data, which is backwards-looking, was supportive of the transaction.
turns.zh: ……对这栋楼的租金、去化和出租率采取了远为保守的假设，最终让我们在这笔交易上不再具竞争力——尽管所有公开可得的市场数据，那些向后看的数据，都是支持这笔交易的。

turns.en: With all of the internal relationships in Invesco, I'd love to hear more about who is adjacent to you that's helping foster in this information when you're looking to underwrite alone. We're fortunate to have a lot of internal experts. This starts at the macro level. My view as a real estate lender is that my job is to be building and managing a portfolio which should perform throughout all stages of the economic and credit cycle. I believe my investors are
turns.zh: 在 Invesco 有这么多内部关系，我很想多听听：当你承保一笔贷款时，你旁边都有谁在帮你培育这些信息？——我们很幸运有很多内部专家，这从宏观层面就开始了。我作为房地产贷款人的看法是：我的工作是构建和管理一个应该在经济和信用周期各个阶段都能良好表现的组合。我相信我的投资人……

turns.en: investing with me for that downside protection and an attractive income profile on a through cycle basis. They're not getting total return. They're not getting upside when values are ripping.
turns.zh: ……投资我这一类产品，要的就是那种下行保护和穿越周期的有吸引力的收益流。他们拿不到总回报，估值大涨的时候他们拿不到上行。

turns.en: On the flip side, they should have a much more stable experience in a down cycle. One of the things that we are thinking about is how do we structure our loans and our balance sheet such that we can deliver an attractive yield for our investors in all stages of the rate cycle?
turns.zh: 但反过来，在下行周期里他们应该有远为平稳的体验。我们在思考的一件事是：如何构建我们的贷款和资产负债表，使我们能在利率周期的各个阶段都为投资人提供有吸引力的收益率？

turns.en: We talk about being rate agnostic. That being said, Invesco has a huge fixed income capability. We have major equity capabilities. We have currency capabilities. We are regularly talking to our rate strategists to understand their perspective of where they think rates are going so that we can make sure that we are sensitizing investments in an appropriate way, maybe modulating risk, taking more of a risk on or a risk off posture, depending on that viewpoint.
turns.zh: 我们说要做到利率不可知（rate agnostic）。话虽如此，Invesco 有庞大的固定收益能力、很强的股票能力、也有外汇能力。我们经常和我们的利率策略师交流，了解他们认为利率会往哪里走，以便确保我们用恰当的方式对投资做敏感性分析，也许是在调节风险——根据那个观点采取更进取或更规避风险的姿态。

turns.en: Similarly, we have macro economists who are thinking about major macro trends that can inform where we are thinking about leaning in from a geographic perspective or an industry concentration perspective. When it comes to the real estate, we're a global business.
turns.zh: 类似地，我们有宏观经济学家在思考重大宏观趋势，这些信息可以指导我们从地域角度或行业集中度角度考虑往哪里发力。说到房地产本身，我们是一家全球业务。

turns.en: Many of our borrowers borrow from us in both the United States and in Europe. We are talking to our colleagues on both sides of the Atlantic. I sit on the European credit investment committee. My colleague who runs our European credit business sits on the US committee. We're trying to bring in a variety of expertise across the platform. Within the equity business, we have folks who have specialized on some specific product types. We have a team that
turns.zh: 我们很多借款人在美国和欧洲都向我们借款，我们和大西洋两岸的同事都在交流。我担任欧洲信用投委会的委员，负责我们欧洲信用业务的同事担任美国投委会的委员。我们试图把整个平台的各种专业能力引进来。在股权业务内部，有人专注于某些特定物业类型。我们有专门做……

turns.en: is specialized on single family for rent. We have a team that specialized in medical office, a manufactured housing team, a self storage team. As we see opportunities in those property types, we're pulling them in to help us assess the risk. Make sure we're looking at the right metrics in those markets. Importantly understanding the physical characteristics of buildings. I think back to an example of an industrial property in Phoenix that we were underwriting for multi-repeat
turns.zh: ……独栋出租住宅（SFR）的团队，有专门做医疗写字楼的团队、预制住宅团队、自助仓储团队。当我们在这些物业类型上看到机会时，就把他们拉进来帮我们评估风险，确保我们在那些市场看的是正确的指标，更重要的是理解建筑的物理特征。我想起一个例子：凤凰城的一栋工业物业，我们当时在为一家多次合作的老客户承保……

turns.en: borrower of ours. On paper, it looked like a slam dunk. We owned two industrial buildings in the same sub market. Overall, market sats were pretty healthy in that sub market.
turns.zh: ……的贷款。纸面上看，这是一笔稳赢的交易。我们在同一个子市场自己持有两栋工业物业，总体来看那个子市场的空置率相当健康。

turns.en: When we brought in our asset manager, who's been asset managing industrial in Phoenix for 25 years and sits in our local office here in Southern California, she said immediately, I wouldn't do that deal. That is the last in first out building in the market. The reasons are, one, it doesn't have as good of truck parking as the other buildings in the market. That's always going to be a consideration for tenants in this market.
turns.zh: 当我们请来我们的资产管理者——她在凤凰城做工业资产管理已经 25 年，就坐在我们在南加州的本地办公室——她立刻说：我不会做那笔交易。那是市场上最后进场、最先出场的楼。原因一是，它的卡车车位不如市场上其他楼那么好，在这个市场，这永远是租户会掂量的因素。

turns.en: Two, the specific micro location real estate being a block by block building by building business means that trucks need to make three left turns coming off the interstate to get to that building. If tenants can go into a building where they only need to make one left turn or right turns, they're going to save a minute, 90 seconds every time that adds up over the years in diesel fuel costs, they're going to go to those buildings first.
turns.zh: 二是具体的微区位。房地产是一个逐街区、逐楼栋的生意，这意味着卡车下了州际高速要左拐三次才能到那栋楼。如果租户能去一栋只需要拐一次弯、或者都是右拐就能进场的楼，每次就能省一分钟、90 秒，一年年累积下来就是柴油成本，他们就会优先去那些楼。

turns.en: When you go through this loan by loan, you make decisions to underwrite certain things that come on your plate. How do you think about constructing a portfolio of loans?
turns.zh: 当你逐笔审批来到你面前的交易时，你会做出承保哪些东西的决定。你怎么思考构建一个贷款组合？

turns.en: It is one of the more important things that we need to think about as I think back on lessons learned from the last correction, which by the way, the correction in commercial real estate between 22 and 23 was one of the three most severe corrections in commercial real estate in modern history since World War II. I have honed in on that experience on making sure we continue to have strong discipline around minimizing concentration risk within our portfolio. From a credit perspective,
turns.zh: 回头想想上一轮调整中学到的教训，这是我们必须思考的最重要的事情之一——顺带一提，22 到 23 年的商业地产调整，是自二战以来现代史上最严重的前三次商业地产调整之一。我特别从那段经历中聚焦于一点：确保我们在把组合内集中度风险降到最低上，始终保持强有力的纪律。从信用角度……

turns.en: I am much more sensitive to that concentration risk than maybe I would be in an equity portfolio. Certainly a higher yielding equity portfolio where I may make some concentrated bets.
turns.zh: ……我对集中度风险要比在股权组合里敏感得多，当然，在一个更高收益的股权组合里，我可能会做一些集中的押注。

turns.en: Being focused on preservation of capital and minimizing downside risk, I want to make sure that if there's a Black Swan event at a single asset, that that doesn't have a significant negative impact on the overall portfolio. Diversification comes across multiple metrics. It's geographic diversification. It's underlying tenant industry diversification, making sure we don't have too much exposure with any given sponsor in any given fund, property types, currency in our global funds.
turns.zh: 但专注于保全资本和把下行风险降到最低，我要确保如果单一资产出现黑天鹅事件，它不会对整体组合产生重大负面影响。分散化体现在多个维度：地理分散，底层租户行业分散，确保我们在任何一只基金里对任何单一发起人的敞口不超标，还有物业类型、以及全球基金里的币种。

turns.en: From there, portfolio construction is less sensitive than you would see in some total return strategies. The most important thing is making sure that we're not taking binary downside risks or going to look at making sure that we have exposure to those property types that are generally aligned with the convictions that we have from a top down for real estate equity.
turns.zh: 在此基础上，组合构建的敏感度会低于你在全回报策略里看到的。最重要的是确保我们不赌二元下行风险，同时去看我们的敞口是否大体上与我们自上而下对房地产股权的信念一致。

turns.en: As you're monitoring portfolio, inevitably real estate cyclical, you will go through a tough market. You mentioned that 22, 23, one of the toughest that you've seen. When things start going wrong, how do you think about triaging where the problems are first, understanding what you need to do as the manager of those loans? We have a couple of fundamental principles.
turns.zh: 当你在监控组合的时候，房地产不可避免是周期性的，你会经历艰难的市场。你提到 22、23 年是你见过的最艰难的市场之一。当事情开始出问题时，你怎么思考分诊、先弄清问题在哪里，作为这些贷款的管理人需要做什么？

turns.en: One is, we are a relationship lender. We're in this business for win-win transactions. If we have a loan where the underlying collateral is experiencing some challenges, we are generally going to take the position of working with our borrowers, giving them more time so long as they are evidencing that they are committed to the asset, that they are committing resources, attention to the execution of the business plan, also committing capital to the deal.
turns.zh: ——我们有几条基本原则。一是，我们是关系型贷款人，我们做这门生意是为了双赢的交易。如果我们有笔贷款，其底层抵押物正遇到困难，我们通常会站在与借款人共同解决的立场上，给他们更多时间——只要他们在证明：他们致力于这个资产，正在投入资源和注意力去执行商业计划，也在往交易里投入资本。

turns.en: If they are, we're going to lean in generally on giving them more time. If they're not, we're going to move swiftly because we don't want to see waste at the property.
turns.zh: 如果他们做到了，我们通常会倾向于给他们更多时间。如果没有，我们就会快速行动，因为我们不想看到物业被糟蹋。

turns.en: We have the ability typically to exercise remedies, take control of a property in 60 to 90 days in most jurisdictions. We can do that with some degree of certainty.
turns.zh: 在大多数司法管辖区，我们通常有能力在 60 到 90 天内行使救济手段、接管一处物业，这一点我们可以在相当程度上确定地做到。

turns.en: In many instances, that credible threat is sufficient in getting some borrowers' attention. In the COVID time period, we had six hotel loans. We quickly got with all of our hotel borrowers in five out of six instances. They either said, it's tough times. We're going to keep going.
turns.zh: 很多时候，这种可信的威慑本身就足以让某些借款人重视起来。新冠疫情期间，我们有六笔酒店贷款，我们迅速与所有酒店借款人沟通。六笔里有五笔，他们要么说：这是艰难时刻，我们要撑下去，

turns.en: We're going to inject capital. We believe in this asset. Please be patient with us. Or could you give us some modest accommodations, maybe a crew interest so we don't have to be coming out of pocket for three months of this period? We had one borrower who took a much firmer position and said, Imbesco, we want you to fully accrue interest for a year.
turns.zh: 我们要注资，我们相信这个资产，请对我们有耐心。要么说：能不能给我们一点通融，比如利息资本化（accrued interest），让我们在头三个月不用自掏腰包？我们有一个借款人采取了远为强硬的立场，说：Invesco，我们要求你们全额计收一年的利息。

turns.en: By the way, occupancy has gone from 85% to two occupied rooms. We still have taxes, insurance, utilities, and labor to pay. We want you to come out of pocket to pay those operating costs.
turns.zh: 顺便说一下，出租率已经从 85% 掉到只剩两间客房有人。我们还是要付税、保险、水电和人工，我们要你们自掏腰包来付这些运营成本。

turns.en: Our answer was, that's fine. If that's your position, we'll do that. Our investors need to benefit from the upside if we're increasing our exposure at this difficult time. We commenced a foreclosure process a week before the foreclosure. We got a liquor license, so those two people in the hotel could have some beverages. Our borrower realized we were serious and they paid us off in full in July of 2020. I have to think we were one of the only hotel
turns.zh: 我们的回答是：没问题，如果那是你的立场，我们就这么做。如果我们在这个艰难时刻加大敞口，我们的投资人需要分享上行。我们在止赎（foreclosure）前一周启动了止赎流程，还办了一张酒类牌照，好让酒店里那两位住客能喝点东西。我们的借款人意识到我们是认真的，在 2020 年 7 月把我们全额偿还了。我想我们大概是极少数在 2020 年被全额清偿的酒店……

turns.en: lenders to be paid off in full in 2020. How do you work through a relationship in a situation like that where maybe they were anomalous relative to the other ones? How do you reassess that at a tough time? It's the classic adage of in trying times, you see partners true colors. That specific example was a borrower who we'd done seven loans with. I like the people there. I still consider them to be friends, but we saw how they approach things with their lenders. That's not what we
turns.zh: ……贷款人之一。在那种情况下，也许这个借款人相对于其他家是异类，你怎么处理一段关系？你怎么在艰难时刻重新评估它？——有句老话：患难见真情。那个具体的例子是一个和我们做过七笔贷款的借款人。我喜欢那里的人，我仍然把他们当作朋友，但我们看到了他们对待贷款人的方式。那不是我们……

turns.en: expect from our borrowers, so we're not going to make another loan to them and we haven't. There are a couple of borrowers out there who had tough situations. They did the right thing all along. You could take the posture of, hey, if you've lent to someone and the underlying business plan was a failure, maybe you shouldn't lend to them again. We have the entirely opposite view. We're going to lean in for those borrowers who leaned in for us.
turns.zh: ……期望借款人有的样子，所以我们不会再给他们放款，也确实没有。外面也有几个借款人当时处境艰难，但他们一路都做了正确的事。你也许会持这种态度：如果你借给了某个人，而底层商业计划失败了，也许你不该再借给他们。我们则完全相反：对于那些在我们需要时挺过我们的借款人，我们会加倍向他们靠拢。

turns.en: In an asset class that you're participating in, there is so much data in this exploding world of AI. Chris, how you've used AI to enhance the information that you have.
turns.zh: 在你所参与的这类资产里，在这个 AI 爆炸的世界中有海量的数据。Charlie，你们是怎么用 AI 来增强你们掌握的信息的？

turns.en: We are an AI-first organization. We are moving swiftly. We are investing heavily in AI applications and uses. This is a top-down mandate for the firm. Our objectives are to use AI to optimize investment outcomes to improve our investor experience. You'll notice that efficiencies and saving costs aren't one of the top two objectives. Maybe that will be something that we can benefit from in the future. We are using AI constantly. There is a healthy
turns.zh: 我们是一家 AI 优先的组织，行动很快，在 AI 应用和用途上大力投入，这是自上而下的公司级任务。我们的目标是：用 AI 优化投资结果、改善投资人体验。你会注意到，提效和降本并不在前两大目标之列——也许那是未来我们可以顺带享受的红利。我们一直在使用 AI。我们内部有一种健康的……

turns.en: tension within our organization of leaders pushing hard for innovation and increased adoption while compliance and legal are putting up healthy guardrails around that. Our client's data must be preserved. We certainly can't have AI agents making investment decisions or presenting faulty information that is used for investment decisions. There are many, many different applications that we're using on a daily basis. We're using AI to create lease abstracts to take
turns.zh: ……张力：领导层大力推动创新和更多采纳，而合规与法务则为此设置健康的护栏。我们客户的数据必须受到保护，我们当然不能让 AI 代理做投资决策，或者提供有缺陷的信息被用于投资决策。我们每天使用许许多多不同的应用：我们用 AI 生成租约摘要，把……

turns.en: 100-page leases, summarize them down to the key points that our underwriters need. We're using AI to do some modeling tasks. We are using AI as a basic research assistant tool for us. We are automating much of our investor reporting with AI agents its early days for us in our implementation of AI. As you look at your opportunity set as it comes across your desk, what are some of the things that you are finding interesting that you think the market may not?
turns.zh: ……100 页的租约浓缩成承保人员需要的关键点；我们用 AI 做一些建模任务；我们把 AI 当作基础研究助手；我们用 AI 代理自动化大量投资人报告。我们落地 AI 还处于早期。——看看来到你面前的机会集，有哪些是你觉得有意思、而市场可能还没注意到的？

turns.en: We have taken a constructive position on Europe that has been a differentiator relative to some of our peer sets. We see that we can at times generate some excess yield for like-kind risk in Europe given greater information asymmetry in that market. You also see us legging into adjacent property types to our two major themes. We've been a long-standing player in industrial outdoor storage and self-storage. Those are areas where we have significant exposure and we're
turns.zh: 我们对欧洲持积极的立场，相对于我们的一些同行，这是一个差异化。我们看到在欧洲，由于那个市场存在更大的信息不对称，我们有时能为同等风险争取到一些超额收益。你们也会看到我们在两大主题的相邻物业类型上逐步铺开。我们在工业露天仓储（IOS）和自助仓储已经做了很久，这些领域我们敞口很大，而且在持续……

turns.en: continuing to gain exposure in the sheds portion of the beds and sheds. I would include iOS and self-storage as sheds category. On the bedside, we are active in conventional multifamily.
turns.zh: ……增加 beds and sheds 里 sheds 一侧的敞口。我会把 IOS 和自助仓储都归入 sheds 这一类。在 beds 这一侧，我们在常规多户住宅很活跃。

turns.en: We also have been active in 55-plus age-restricted communities. Student housing recently has been a major theme of ours. You have to be careful in student housing because these individual markets are relatively small. They can be exposed to excess supply, but if you pick the right locations, they can be fortress assets. We think about how are we able to create different access pathways to opportunity? One area where we've invested a lot of time and built a healthy architecture
turns.zh: 我们也在 55 岁以上的年龄限制型长者社区很活跃。学生公寓最近是我们的一个重要主题。学生公寓要谨慎，因为单个市场相对较小，可能面临供给过剩；但如果你选对位置，它们可以是堡垒型资产。我们会思考：如何创造出通往机会的不同通道？我们花了很多时间并建立了成熟架构的一个领域，是……

turns.en: is in creating standby portfolio facilities. For our borrowers who are pursuing aggregation strategies, we'll set up a $250-$300-$500 million facility with specific parameters that's on standby.
turns.zh: ……设立备用组合额度（standby portfolio facility）。对于在做资产聚合策略的借款人，我们会搭一个 2.5 亿、3 亿到 5 亿美元规模、带特定参数的备用额度。

turns.en: It gives our borrowers certainty of execution from a credit underwriting perspective as they're pursuing new opportunities, efficient financing process when they onboard new opportunities, and gives us access to some transactions that we wouldn't otherwise have access to.
turns.zh: 它让借款人在追逐新机会时，从信用承保角度获得执行的确定性，在纳入新机会时拥有高效的融资流程，同时也让我们得以进入一些本来接触不到的交易。

turns.en: How do you set the bounds to make sure that when the time comes for that investor to access the loan that you're comfortable with it? A lot of good communication, making sure that everyone has a clear and unified vision for the purpose of the facility. We have full discretion over any loan that gets added to the facility. You want it to be a win-win transaction. It's not in anyone's interest for us to spend a bunch of time setting up a facility and then not approve loans,
turns.zh: 你们怎么划定边界，确保当那个借款人需要提取贷款时，你会乐意接受这笔贷款？——很多好的沟通，确保每个人都对额度的目的有清晰、统一的认知。对进入额度的任何一笔贷款，我们都拥有完全的裁量权。要让它成为双赢交易：如果我们花很多时间搭一个额度、回头却不批贷款，那对谁都没好处。……

turns.en: making sure that there is alignment on what fits and doesn't fit early on is critical. How are you thinking about the influx of interest from private wealth?
turns.zh: ……早期就在什么合适、什么不合适上达成一致，这一点至关重要。——你们怎么看私人财富资金的涌入？

turns.en: Invesco is most known as a traditional asset manager. We're one of the four largest managers of ETFs globally. We have a successful, actively managed mutual fund franchise. We have a huge exposure to retail investors and deep relationships in those distribution channels.
turns.zh: Invesco 最广为人知的身份还是传统资产管理人。我们是全球四大 ETF 管理人之一，拥有成功的主动管理共同基金业务。我们在零售投资者那边有巨大的触达和深厚的分销渠道关系。

turns.en: One of our strategic initiatives is to take our best ideas on the private market side and bring those to the wealth channel. We've done that in real estate equity. We've done that in private credit. We have done that in real estate credit as well. We did see earlier in the cycle a pretty significant growth of wealth capital on the real estate equity side. There have been a number of entrants on the credit side in recent years, but if you look at the amount of wealth capital raised
turns.zh: 我们的战略举措之一，就是把私募市场端最好的想法带到财富渠道。我们在房地产股权做到了，在私募信用做到了，在房地产信用也做到了。我们确实看到在本周期早些时候，财富资金在房地产股权端有相当显著的增长。信用侧近年也有不少进入者，但如果你看流入房地产信用工具的财富资金总量……

turns.en: into real estate credit vehicles, it is a drop in the bucket relative to the overall market size and is not coming close to filling the gap that is then left by the banks.
turns.zh: ……相对于整个市场规模，那只是沧海一粟，还远远谈不上填补银行退出留下的缺口。

turns.en: You can also look at broader debt fund fundraising. There certainly is activity in that space, both from the wealth channel and the institutional channel. For every new entrant in the debt fund space, we're seeing another group that took some real hits along the way during this last correction who's now out of the market. What excites you as you look out over the next couple years? There was a moment in time during the pandemic where I was stuck in my basement working.
turns.zh: 你也可以看更宽泛的债务基金募资。那个领域确实有活跃度，财富渠道和机构渠道都有。但债务基金领域每进来一个新进入者，我们就能看到另一家在上一轮调整中一路受到重创、如今已退出市场的机构。——当你展望未来几年，什么让你兴奋？疫情期间有那么一段时间，我被困在自家地下室里工作。

turns.en: I live in Los Angeles. Half of my neighbors were in the entertainment industry, and as far as I could tell, they were having fun, relaxing, and not working for those first several months.
turns.zh: 我住在洛杉矶，一半的邻居都在娱乐行业。就我能看到的，在那最初的几个月里，他们在玩乐、放松，不用工作。

turns.en: We were working harder than we'd ever worked before. It felt like I was rolling out of bed, going straight to my home office, cranking until lights out. That was a tough time.
turns.zh: 我们那时比任何时候都辛苦。感觉就是从床上滚下来，直接钻进家庭办公室，一直干到熄灯。那是一段艰难的时光。

turns.en: In some ways, I stumbled into my current role. I had a moment during the pandemic where I looked myself in the mirror and said, is this what I meant to do? Sling real estate loans for large commercial owners of real estate? That helped me form some clarity around what it is that we do. At the end of the day, we are managing money for retirees, future retirees, both the wealth side, DC, defined contribution, also defined benefit. We're managing money for
turns.zh: 某种程度上，我是跌跌撞撞进入现在这个角色的。疫情期间有一个时刻，我对着镜子里的自己说：这是我想做的事吗？给大型商业地产业主兜售房地产贷款？那促使我想清楚了我们到底在做什么。说到底，我们是在为退休人士和未来退休人士管钱——不管是财富端的 DC，固定缴款计划（defined contribution），还是固定收益计划（defined benefit）。我们在为……管钱。

turns.en: insurance companies, and that is enabling insurance companies to pay out on claims for life insurance when there's a tragedy in a family or some other major need. We are providing for these ultimate beneficiaries. It's helpful for us to keep that in mind. On a day-to-day basis, I view my role as providing for my family. I have young kids. I also provide opportunities for our team to provide opportunity for their families. If my colleagues want to put their kids through
turns.zh: ……保险公司管钱，这让保险公司能在家庭遭遇不幸或有其他重大需要时支付人寿保险理赔。我们是在供养这些最终的受益人，时刻记住这一点很有帮助。在日常生活中，我把我的角色看作供养我的家庭。我有年幼的孩子，我也为我们团队创造机会，让他们有机会供养他们的家庭。如果我的同事想让孩子上……

turns.en: private school, making sure that they can do that. If they want to plan an early retirement, plan for a family, whatever it is, it gives me a lot of pleasure to see us creating those opportunities for our people. Over the next several years, we're going to continue to grow this business fairly substantially. Our pace of growth is quick, but governed by our fundamental principle that performance comes first, growth can only come to the extent that we can maintain
turns.zh: ……私立学校，我要确保他们做得到。如果他们想规划提前退休、为家庭做打算，无论是什么——看到我们在为我们的伙伴创造这些机会，让我非常欣慰。未来几年，我们会继续相当大规模地增长这个业务。我们增长的节奏很快，但受一条根本原则的约束：业绩第一，增长只能建立在能够维持……的基础上。

turns.en: our performance position in the marketplace for our clients. Over time, we're going to provide for a whole lot more families here at Invesco Real Estate, and that's exciting.
turns.zh: ……我们为客户在市场中的业绩地位的前提上。假以时日，在 Invesco 房地产，我们会为多得多的家庭提供支撑，这令人兴奋。

turns.en: Try to make sure I get a chance to ask you a couple of closing questions. What's the most rewarding thing you do outside of work? The most rewarding thing that I am doing outside of work is, as a father, I have four young kids.
turns.zh: 尽量让我有机会问你几个收尾的问题。工作之外最有意义的事是什么？——工作之外最有意义的，是为人父这件事。我有四个年幼的孩子。

turns.en: I recently joined the board of my eldest daughter's school, which is an amazing school focused on teaching children with language-based learning differences from grades two through 12.
turns.zh: 我最近加入了大女儿学校的董事会。那是一所很棒的学校，专注教导有语言型学习差异（language-based learning differences）的孩子，从二年级到十二年级。

turns.en: These are kids who the traditional public schools and independent private schools in our region have failed, have been unable to teach these kids how to read and learn and develop a love of learning. Our school is able to cater to these students and teach them in the way they need to be taught. That's incredibly rewarding. What are you unusually good at that most people don't know about? I'm a pretty good skier. Most people don't get to see me doing that. I grew up in that
turns.zh: 这些孩子是我们地区的传统公立学校和私立独立学校没能教好的——没能教会他们如何阅读、如何学习、如何培养对学习的热爱。我们学校能够满足这些学生的需求，用他们需要的方式教导他们。这非常有意义。——你有什么超出常人的、大多数人不知道的拿手好戏？——我滑雪滑得相当好，大多数人看不到我滑。我在那个小镇长大……

turns.en: small town. While it did rain an awful lot, the mountains were only about 35 minutes away. It snowed quite a lot in the mountains. Back then, lift tickets were $12 a day. My mom would pack us brown bag lunches. It was a accessible middle-class support back then and a huge part of my childhood.
turns.zh: ……虽然雨确实下得很多，但山只有大约 35 分钟车程，山上雪下得挺大。那时候缆车票一天 12 美元，我妈会给我们装纸袋午餐。在那个年代，这是中产阶级负担得起的活动，是我童年的重要部分。

turns.en: At Stanford, I joined the ski team, which is nothing to write home about, but meant that I spent a huge amount of time skiing throughout my early life and into my 20s. It's something that I got a lot of joy out of and am enjoying teaching my kids these days. What's your biggest pet peeve?
turns.zh: 在 Stanford 我加入了滑雪队，那不算什么了不得的事，但意味着我早年和二十多岁时花了大量时间滑雪。那件事给了我很多快乐，现在我很享受教我的孩子们滑雪。——你最受不了的事情是什么？

turns.en: My biggest pet peeve is people not getting to the point. I want to hear what you're saying. I want to understand your recommendation and I want you to tell me what you're saying before you go into all of the detail. We're busy around here. I value your opinion. I want you to get it out efficiently. What have you changed your mind about the last few years?
turns.zh: 我最受不了的是别人不直入主题。我想听你在说什么，我想理解你的建议，我希望你先告诉我结论，然后再进入所有细节。我们这儿都很忙，我珍视你的意见，我希望你高效地把它讲出来。——过去几年你在什么事情上改变了看法？

turns.en: This has been a significant time of growth for me as an investor until December of 2022. I had never experienced a realized loss on any investment that I made. In some ways, experiencing that first loss was a liberating experience that has now allowed me to have a much more humble view of myself as an investor. It allowed me to go back and look at not only the investments that went sideways, but also the investments that went well where we were lucky and be honest
turns.zh: 这对我来说是一段作为投资人的重要成长期。直到 2022 年 12 月，我从没在我做的任何一笔投资上体验过已实现亏损。某种程度上，经历那次首亏是一种解放，让我如今对自己作为投资人有更谦卑的看法。它让我能回头审视——不仅看那些走歪的投资，也看那些做得好的、其实有运气成分的投资，并诚实……

turns.en: with myself about why those investments were either successful or not, and realize that the investments that were successful sometimes have lessons for me to learn from.
turns.zh: ……地面对自己：那些投资为什么成功或失败，并且意识到，那些成功的投资有时候也给我留下了值得吸取的教训。

turns.en: Which two people have had the biggest impact on your professional life? Without a doubt, number one is my father, John McBride Rose. My dad started his career in public service when I was a baby. He found himself unemployed. He had to plead for a job with a public finance shop in Seattle. He ended up making an incredible career, financing primarily public schools through bond issuances throughout the Pacific Northwest. He ended up as CEO of that
turns.zh: 哪两个人对你的职业人生影响最大？——毫无疑问，第一位是我的父亲 John McBride Rose。我还是个婴儿的时候，我爸就开始了公职生涯。他一度失业，不得不去恳求西雅图一家市政金融公司给他一份工作。最终他做出了一段了不起的职业生涯，主要通过债券发行为整个太平洋西北地区的公立学校融资，最后做到了那家机构的……

turns.en: organization. My father taught me how critical honesty and ethics are. Above all else, he taught me how important it is to care for the people that you work with and your clients. He did so in a humble lead by example way without being explicit in the way that he taught his lessons. Today, I am inspired by our CEO at Invesco, Andrew Schlossberg. He has set a clear strategic direction for our firm, which is principles-based. I'm excited to see where he takes this firm
turns.zh: ……CEO。我父亲教会我诚实和道德有多重要。最重要的，是他教会我关心与你共事的人和你关心的客户有多重要。他用一种谦逊的身教方式做到这些，而不是把功课讲明白。如今，我们 Invesco 的 CEO Andrew Schlossberg 激励着我。他为我们的公司设定了清晰的战略方向，那是基于原则的。我很期待未来十年……

turns.en: over the next decade. Charlie, last one related to that. If the next five years are a chapter in your life, what's that chapter about? My husband and I have talked a lot about how this is a specific chapter in our lives right now. We moved last year to live close to the school for children with learning differences that my daughter attends. We moved to a great neighborhood with great neighbors, which is not a neighborhood that I would have chosen to live in were it not for
turns.zh: ……他会把这家公司带向哪里。Charlie，最后一个问题跟这个有关。如果未来五年是你人生的一章，这一章是关于什么的？——我和我先生聊了很多，聊到现在正处在人生中特定的一章。我们去年搬了家，住到离我女儿那所学习差异儿童学校更近的地方。我们搬进了一个很好的社区，邻居也很好——如果不是因为……

turns.en: my daughter's educational needs. This is that chapter in our lives where we are parents, we are going all in. There will be a time in my life when I can live in exactly the neighborhood that I want to live in. Charlie, thanks so much for sharing another great chapter in the Invesco story in real estate. Dad, it was a pleasure. I hope we can do it again. Thanks for listening to this sponsored insight. Sponsored episodes are paid opportunities for another 12 to 18 managers a
turns.zh: ……我女儿的教育需求，那并不是我会主动选择的社区。这就是我们人生中作为父母、全力以赴的这一章。我生命中会有那么一个时刻，可以恰恰住在我想住的那个社区。——Charlie，非常感谢你分享了 Invesco 房地产故事的又一精彩篇章。——Ted，很荣幸，希望我们还能再来一次。感谢收听本期赞助洞察。赞助单集是付费机会，每年有另外 12 到 18 家管理人……
